name: BusinessEmailCompromise
description: A case template for handling suspected or confirmed business email compromise incidents, including validation, mailbox analysis, fraud assessment, containment, remediation, communications, and post-incident follow-up.
author: Zachary Carter
summary:
## Incident Report — [CASE TITLE]

## Executive Summary

**[Provide a high-level, non-technical summary suitable for senior leadership. Describe the nature of the incident (e.g. mailbox takeover, vendor impersonation, invoice fraud), how and when it was identified, the scope of affected accounts and parties, fraud exposure, and current response status. Typically two to four paragraphs.]**

## Scope of Investigation

**[Define the boundaries of this investigation — what was in scope, what was explicitly excluded, and any limitations on access or evidence that constrained findings.]**

## Technical Analysis

**[Map investigative findings to the MITRE ATT&CK framework where applicable. Complete each subsection with specific techniques, evidence, and timeline data. Remove tactics where no activity was observed and note the absence explicitly.]**

### TA0001 — Initial Access

**Techniques observed:**

**[e.g. T1566.001 Spearphishing Attachment, T1078 Valid Accounts, T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application]**

**[Describe how the threat actor first gained access — whether through phishing, credential stuffing, token theft, or another method. Include the targeted account, delivery mechanism, and timestamp of first known access.]**

| Date/Time (UTC) | Technique | Account / Host | Description | Evidence Source |
|-----------------|-----------|---------------|-------------|----------------|
| | | | | |

### TA0003 — Persistence

**Techniques observed:**

**[e.g. T1137.005 Outlook Rules, T1098.003 Additional Cloud Roles, T1550.001 Application Access Token]**

**[Describe mechanisms used to maintain access or monitor the mailbox — inbox rules, forwarding rules, delegate permissions, OAuth grants, or additional account changes.]**

| Account | Mechanism | Detail | Date Created | Status |
|---------|-----------|--------|--------------|--------|
| | Inbox rule / Forwarding rule / Delegate / OAuth grant / Other | | | Confirmed / Removed / Pending |

### TA0005 — Defense Evasion

**Techniques observed:**

**[e.g. T1070.008 Clear Mailbox Data, T1036 Masquerading, T1564.008 Email Hiding Rules]**

**[Describe techniques used to avoid detection — deletion of sent items, hiding rules, use of legitimate services, or suppression of alert notifications to the victim.]**

| Date/Time (UTC) | Technique | Account | Description | Evidence Source |
|-----------------|-----------|---------|-------------|----------------|
| | | | | |

### TA0006 — Credential Access

**Techniques observed:**

**[e.g. T1111 MFA Interception, T1528 Steal Application Access Token, T1539 Steal Web Session Cookie]**

**[Document how the threat actor acquired or maintained valid credentials — phishing pages, token theft, MFA bypass, or session hijacking.]**

| Date/Time (UTC) | Technique | Account | Method | Evidence Source |
|-----------------|-----------|---------|--------|----------------|
| | | | | |

### TA0009 — Collection

**Techniques observed:**

**[e.g. T1114.002 Remote Email Collection, T1114.001 Local Email Collection]**

**[Describe any evidence of the threat actor reading, searching, or exporting mailbox content — including access to finance threads, banking correspondence, or sensitive business communications.]**

| Date/Time (UTC) | Account | Content Accessed | Method | Evidence Source |
|-----------------|---------|-----------------|--------|----------------|
| | | | | |

### TA0011 — Command and Control

**Techniques observed:**

**[e.g. T1071.003 Mail Protocols, T1102 Web Service]**

**[Document any attacker-controlled infrastructure used — lookalike domains, reply-to addresses, attacker-controlled mailboxes, or OAuth applications used to maintain persistent access.]**

| Indicator | Type | First Seen (UTC) | Last Seen (UTC) | Evidence Source |
|-----------|------|-----------------|----------------|----------------|
| | Lookalike domain / Reply-to address / OAuth app / IP | | | |

### TA0040 — Impact to Entity

**Techniques observed:**

**[e.g. T1657 Financial Theft, T1496 Resource Hijacking]**

**[Document the final-stage fraud actions taken — fraudulent payment instructions issued, banking details changed, payroll redirected, gift card requests made, or other business process abuse. Include the point at which any payment or change was actioned.]**

| Date/Time (UTC) | Action | Target / Victim | Amount / Impact | Fraud Executed? | Evidence Source |
|-----------------|--------|----------------|----------------|----------------|----------------|
| | Wire request / Banking change / Payroll redirect / Gift card / Other | | | Yes / No / Partial | |

---

## Remediation & Recommendations

### Immediate Actions

| # | Action | Owner | Priority | Due |
|---|--------|-------|----------|-----|
| 1 | Reset credentials and revoke all active sessions for affected accounts | | Critical | |
| 2 | Remove malicious inbox rules, forwarding rules, and delegate permissions | | Critical | |
| 3 | Revoke unauthorised OAuth application grants | | Critical | |
| 4 | Block lookalike domains and malicious sender addresses at the mail gateway | | Critical | |
| 5 | Suspend pending payment or banking change requests pending verification | | Critical | |
| 6 | Initiate wire recall with financial institutions if fraudulent payment executed | | Critical | |

### Strategic Improvements

| # | Recommendation | Category | Priority |
|---|---------------|----------|----------|
| 1 | Enforce phishing-resistant MFA across all accounts, prioritising finance and executive staff | Identity | High |
| 2 | Tighten DMARC policy to p=reject and enable lookalike domain monitoring | Email security | High |
| 3 | Formalise call-back verification procedure for all payment and banking change requests | Process | High |
| 4 | Implement dual-approval controls for banking detail changes and high-value payments | Process | High |
| 5 | Enable mailbox audit logging and inbox rule creation alerts for all accounts | Detection | High |
| 6 | Restrict OAuth app consent to admin-approved applications only | Identity | Medium |
| 7 | Deliver targeted BEC awareness training to finance, payroll, and executive support staff | Awareness | Medium |

---

## Conclusion

**[Closing summary reinforcing key findings, fraud outcome, and path forward. Suitable for sharing with executive leadership alongside Section 1. Address: the attack method and impersonation technique, whether account compromise occurred, the fraud exposure and recovery outcome, and confidence in containment and remediation.]**

tasks.title: Validate and classify reported BEC activity
tasks.description: Determine whether the reported activity is business email compromise, mailbox takeover, vendor impersonation, executive impersonation, thread hijacking, invoice fraud, payroll fraud, gift card fraud, or a false positive. Distinguish between spoofed-email scenarios and true account compromise.

tasks.title: Preserve email and account evidence
tasks.description: Preserve relevant emails, headers, message traces, mailbox audit logs, sign-in logs, forwarding rules, delegate permissions, inbox rules, sent items, deleted items, OAuth grants, and other artifacts needed to establish a defensible timeline and support fraud analysis.

tasks.title: Identify affected accounts, mailboxes, and parties
tasks.description: Determine which user accounts, mailboxes, distribution groups, aliases, vendors, customers, executives, finance staff, or external correspondents are affected. Document confirmed and suspected scope.

tasks.title: Analyze message content, headers, and delivery path
tasks.description: Analyze message headers, sender identity, reply-to values, authentication results, routing details, display name abuse, impersonation indicators, and conversation context to determine how the fraud attempt or compromise was carried out.

tasks.title: Assess mailbox compromise and persistence
tasks.description: Determine whether the mailbox or account was compromised by reviewing suspicious sign-ins, MFA events, session activity, inbox rules, forwarding rules, delegate access, mailbox permissions, OAuth app consent, and sent-mail behavior.

tasks.title: Assess fraud exposure and financial risk
tasks.description: Determine whether fraudulent payment requests, banking changes, wire instructions, invoice changes, payroll changes, gift card requests, or other financial or business-process abuse occurred. Identify any actual or attempted loss and affected business processes.

tasks.title: Contain malicious emails, accounts, and forwarding mechanisms
tasks.description: Remove or quarantine malicious messages, disable malicious inbox or forwarding rules, revoke sessions and tokens, disable or restrict affected accounts if needed, block malicious senders or lookalike domains, and restrict other identified access paths.

tasks.title: Remediate affected identities and mailbox settings
tasks.description: Reset passwords, revoke sessions, review and re-enroll MFA where needed, remove unauthorized delegates, remove malicious app grants, clean mailbox rules, validate mailbox settings, and ensure control of the affected account has been restored.

tasks.title: Coordinate with finance, HR, legal, and management
tasks.description: Coordinate investigative and response actions with finance, accounts payable, payroll, HR, legal, privacy, and management as appropriate to assess fraud exposure, authorize response steps, and guide communications or notification decisions.

tasks.title: Attempt transaction recovery and external coordination if needed
tasks.description: If fraudulent payments or banking changes occurred, coordinate urgent recovery actions with financial institutions, payment processors, law enforcement, insurers, and affected third parties as appropriate. Document all timing and actions taken.

tasks.title: Notify affected users and stakeholders
tasks.description: Notify affected users, service desk staff, messaging administrators, finance teams, executives, vendors, customers, or other stakeholders as appropriate. Provide clear instructions for validation of requests, password resets, call-back verification, and follow-up actions.

tasks.title: Improve detections, controls, and awareness
tasks.description: Update detection logic, mailbox auditing, alerting, email security controls, domain protections, conditional access, vendor payment validation procedures, callback verification practices, and user awareness content based on findings from the incident.

tasks.title: Document findings and close case
tasks.description: Document the affected accounts, impersonation method, compromise status, fraud exposure, containment actions, remediation steps, transaction recovery efforts, business impact, and lessons learned. Confirm required actions are complete before case closure.
